Open Start and type your company name and your own limits in the yellow cells: target rate per km, cost per km, target margin, free waiting hours, waiting charge, fuel base price and the idle days.
Check Trucks, Trailers and Drivers, then Customers with their terms and Lanes with the usual km, rate and empty km. The break-even rate of each lane fills in.
Enter every load on Loads. Total, revenue per km, profit and the late and margin checks fill in by themselves.
Use Rate Quotes for every offer you give or get, and read Quote Win Rate to see which customers and lanes you win on price.
Keep Rate Confirmations next to the loads: the check shows extras billed beyond what was agreed and loads billed under the agreement.
Log long waits on Waiting Time Log and other extras on Extra Charges. The amounts still to bill show in red until you fill the billed date.
Plan the week on Dispatch Board and Truck Availability. A truck with two loads on one day and a truck idle too long are flagged.
Track appointments, late loads, empty km, backhaul searches and load documents on their sheets; the proof of delivery tracker lists what is missing.
Set your fuel price bands on Fuel Surcharge Schedule and compare them with the formula from your base price.
Keep the Weekly Dispatch Summary current to see revenue per truck day against the four-week average.

Use the 14 calculators before you book: load profit, break-even, rate for a margin, fuel surcharge, empty km, two loads, waiting time, trip days, driving hours, truck day revenue, counter-offer, unloading, rate cut and what-if.
Print 10 sheets and 10 documents, follow 10 checklists and tap a message link to open a chat with the text already written (28 messages).
Read Dispatch Dashboard and Charts every week: loads, revenue per km, empty km, waiting time, late loads and quote results.

One row per invoice: load, customer, dates and amount; days to invoice, days to pay, days overdue, open amount, short amount, status and the chase flag fill in by themselves.
Invoice lines: the charges on each invoice
One row per invoice with the load charges that make it up; the line total and the check against the invoice amount fill in so a charge left off is seen before the invoice goes out.
One row per customer: open invoices split into current, 1 to 30, 31 to 60 and over 60 days overdue, plus the total open and the share over 60 days; all fill in from the Invoices sheet.
Payments received and matched to invoices
One row per payment from a customer or a factoring provider; the invoice amount, the difference and the matched or unmatched flag fill in so a lump payment is allocated before month end.
Short pays and disputes with the amount still short
One row per invoice paid short: billed, paid, reason and what was recovered later; the short amount, the amount still short and the chase flag fill in by themselves.
Customers with terms, credit limit and payment behaviour
One row per broker or direct shipper with terms and credit limit; invoices, average days to pay, days over terms, open and overdue value, revenue and a payment rating fill in from the other sheets.
One row per customer: the limit, the open invoices, the loads on the road not yet invoiced and the room left; the used share and the warning fill in so a new load is not booked over a limit.
Loads on the road, not invoiced
Factoring rate card: fee by days financed
One row per provider and fee step: advance rate and fee by days; the cash per 1,000 and the yearly cost of each step fill in so the providers can be compared.
Factoring advances with fee, days financed and reserve
One row per invoice sold to a factoring provider for an advance; the advance, the reserve, the fee, the days financed and the reserve still due fill in by themselves.
Reserve releases with the fee deducted
One row per reserve paid back by a factoring provider after the customer paid; the fee deducted, the share returned and the days after payment fill in so a short release is seen.
One row per month: invoices sold, their value, the advances, the fees and the reserve paid back; the cost as a share of the factored value and the factored share of all invoicing fill in.
Collections log: every call about a late invoice
One row per call or message about a late invoice: customer, contact, outcome and the date promised; the invoice amount, what is still open and whether the promise was kept fill in by themselves.
One row per delivered load that could not be invoiced because a document was missing; the days held, the interest lost while waiting and the open or complete flag fill in by themselves.
Revenue and cash by customer and month
One row per customer and month: invoices issued, the amount invoiced, invoices paid and the cash received; the customer share of that month fills in by itself.
One row per lane and month: loads and revenue; the revenue per load fills in so a lane that earns less per load stands out.
Extras still to bill: waiting time, unloading fees
One row per extra charge: waiting time, unloading fee paid at the dock, extra stop or cancelled load fee; the billed flag, the amount still to bill and the days it has waited fill in by themselves.
Broker credit checks with the next review
One row per credit check of a new or renewed customer: limit given, rating and next review date; the latest check, the review warning and the change against today's limit fill in by themselves.
Quick-pay offers: discount for faster payment
One row per offer of a discount for paying sooner; the discount in money, its yearly cost and the worth-it verdict fill in by themselves.
Cash expected from receivables over the next 12 weeks
One row per week: cash expected from open invoices, from loads not yet booked and reserve releases; the weekly total and the running total fill in so the owner sees the weeks that need a bridge.

Hello, invoice {invoice_id} for load {load_id} is attached. Amount {amount}, due on {due_date}. Please confirm you received it.
Hello, a reminder that invoice {invoice_id} for {amount} is due on {due_date}. Please tell us the payment date.
Hello, invoice {invoice_id} for {amount} is {days_overdue} days overdue. Please pay today or tell us the date we can expect the payment.
Hello {contact}, invoice {invoice_id} of {invoice_amount}: you promised payment by {promised_date}. Please confirm the date.
Customer: final notice, loads on hold
Hello {contact}, {overdue_value} is overdue and the oldest invoice is {max_overdue} days late. New loads are on hold until it is paid.
Hello, your payment of {paid_amount} for invoice {invoice_id} was short by {short_amount}. Please pay the difference or tell us the reason.
Customer: waiting time to be billed
Hello, the waiting time on load {load_id} of {amount} will be on the invoice. Please confirm you accept it.
Hello {contact}, your open value with us is {open_value}, of which {overdue_value} is overdue. A statement is attached.
Hello, the proof of delivery for invoice {invoice_id}, load {load_id}, is attached. Please tell us if anything is missing.
Hello, we offer a discount of {discount_amount} on a typical invoice if you pay {days_gained} days sooner. Please tell us if this suits you.
Hello, we review your credit limit on {next_review}. The limit is now {limit_given}. Please send your latest payment record.
Hello, we received your payment of {amount} on {date}. Thank you.
Hello {contact}, our payment details have changed. Please use only the details on our latest invoice and call us to confirm them before you pay.
Hello, invoice {invoice_id} of {invoice_amount} is assigned to {provider}. Please pay {provider} and not us. The details are on the invoice.
Hello, we submitted invoice {invoice_id} for {invoice_amount} for an advance on {advance_date}. Please confirm you have it.
Hello, please confirm the advance of {advance_amount} for invoice {invoice_id}. Customer: {customer}.
Hello, the reserve of {reserve_held} for invoice {invoice_id} is due. The customer paid on {customer_paid_on}. Please release it.
Hello, {customer} paid invoice {invoice_id} on {customer_paid_on}. Please release the reserve of {reserve_due} now.
Provider: the fee looks too high
Hello, the fee on invoice {invoice_id} is {fee_amount} after {days_financed} days. That looks too high. Please send the fee calculation.
Provider: stop advances on a customer
Hello, please stop advances on invoices of {customer}. Invoice {invoice_id} is the last one we submit for them.
Hello, {customer} has {over60} overdue by more than 60 days, out of {total_open} open. Please decide the next step.
Hello, {name} pays on average {avg_days} days against {terms_days} days of terms. Open value {open_value}.
Hello, factoring in the month of {month} cost {fees} on {factored_value} of invoices. Reserve paid back {reserve_back}.
Hello, cash expected in the week of {week} is {total_expected}; running total {running}. Please check it against your safety cash.
Hello, please approve the credit limit for {customer}: limit {credit_limit}, exposure {exposure}, room left {room_left}.
Hello, payment {payment_id} of {amount} from {customer} arrived on {date}. Please match it to the invoice.
Hello, invoice {invoice_id} for {amount} was issued to {customer} on {invoice_date}. Please record it.
Dispatcher: hold loads for a customer
Hello, please hold new loads for {name}: {overdue_value} is overdue and the oldest invoice is {max_overdue} days late.
To {col:invoices.customer}. Load {col:invoices.load_id}, delivered on {col:invoices.delivery_date}. The proof of delivery is attached.
Amount due: {col:invoices.amount}. Due date: {col:invoices.due_date}. Waiting time over the free hours, unloading fees paid for you and extra stops are part of the amount.
Please quote the invoice number when you pay.
To {col:customers.name}, attention {col:customers.contact}. Terms are {col:customers.terms_days} days and your credit limit is {col:customers.credit_limit}.
Open value: {col:customers.open_value}. Of this, overdue: {col:customers.overdue_value}. The oldest overdue invoice is {col:customers.max_overdue} days past its due date.
Please check the list of invoices attached and tell us about any difference within a few days.
Schedule of invoices of {set:company} offered to {col:advances.provider}, dated {col:advances.advance_date}.
We ask for an advance of {col:advances.advance_amount} at the advance rate of {col:advances.advance_rate}. The reserve of {col:advances.reserve_amount} is held until the customer pays.
Please confirm the advance and the fee rate of {col:advances.fee_pct} in writing.

To {col:invoices.customer}. Invoice {col:invoices.invoice_id} for load {col:invoices.load_id} was due on {col:invoices.due_date}. The amount of {col:invoices.amount} is {col:invoices.days_overdue} days overdue.
If you have paid already, please send us the payment date. If not, please pay now or tell us the date we can expect the payment.
Final notice before a stop on loads
To {col:customers.name}, attention {col:customers.contact}. An amount of {col:customers.overdue_value} is overdue and the oldest invoice is {col:customers.max_overdue} days past its due date.
If we do not receive the payment or a written payment plan within a few days, we will not accept new loads from you until the account is up to date.
We would prefer to keep working with you. Please call us today.
To {col:shortpay.customer}, invoice {col:shortpay.invoice_id}. We billed {col:shortpay.billed} and received {col:shortpay.paid}, which is {col:shortpay.short_amount} short.
The reason noted on your payment was: {col:shortpay.reason}. The charges on the invoice were agreed and the proof of delivery was sent with it.
Please pay the difference of {col:shortpay.still_short} or send us your written reason.
